offerBox.termsOnRequestNote: Ticket size, cycle length, target return, fees, and payout timing vary per ranch and can’t be published here for legal reasons. Available on request — get the investor pack or book a call.

isThisReal.elTapirIntro: El Tapir is our own farm in Paraguay’s Gran Chaco — not a partner ranch, ours. It’s open to visitors by appointment.

whoBuysAtEnd.body: Orbolo’s trading desk is the buyer. Every herd has a buyer lined up before it’s bought, at market prices — you’re never left holding cattle with nowhere to sell them.

whatIfNotEnough.releaseRuleBody: A ranch releases for deployment once 60% of its threshold is committed under signed, unexpired Letters of Intent. Below that, no capital is called from anyone.
whatIfNotEnough.loiExpiryBody: A Letter of Intent expires automatically 90 days after signing. If a ranch hasn’t reached 60% by then, it either stays open for new commitments or is marked withdrawn — either way, you’re notified.

categories.label: Animal loss
categories.body: Cattle can be lost to disease, predation, or accident.

categories.label: Drought
categories.body: Paraguay’s dry season varies year to year, and a severe drought can affect grazing.

categories.label: Currency
categories.body: Returns involve currency exposure between Guaraníes and your own currency.

categories.label: Policy and export
categories.body: Export markets and trade policy can shift over a cycle’s length.

categories.label: Liquidity
categories.body: A Remote Rancher commitment is not a liquid, tradeable asset — your capital is committed for the cycle length.

whatIfWrong.dataRoomNote: Specific provisions and arrangements for each of these risks are documented in the full, NDA-gated data room — available once you sign an NDA.

steps.body: Choose a ranch from the Deployment Pipeline.
Get the investor pack for an overview, then request full data-room access under NDA.
Sign a Letter of Intent — non-binding, and no capital is called yet.
The ranch releases for deployment once 60% of its threshold is committed under signed, unexpired Letters of Intent.
Capital is called only after release. Our Paraguayan operating company buys and tags the animals in your name.
The ranch raises your animals under the Orbolo Code until the cycle closes.
Orbolo’s trading desk sells the beef at market prices, and your return is paid out.

whatYouOwn.body: You own specific animals, tracked by ear tag, under a management agreement with our Paraguayan operating company — not land, and not a share in a fund. Any carbon or biodiversity credits generated stay with the land and the group; your return comes from the beef.

whoVerifies.codeReferenceNote: Every animal is raised under the Orbolo Code.

items.question: Do I need to visit Paraguay to own cattle here?
items.answer: No. You can own tagged animals on a working ranch without ever visiting — though you’re welcome to, by appointment.

items.question: How do I know the animals actually exist?
items.answer: Each animal is tagged and tracked individually. Verification details are available once you request the investor pack.

items.question: Can I exit early?
items.answer: Remote Rancher is a committed-cycle product — it isn’t designed for early exit. Ask about your specific situation when you contact us.

items.question: Who’s eligible to invest?
items.answer: Eligibility depends on where you’re based and other factors. Contact us to find out if you’re eligible.

items.question: What happens when the cycle ends?
items.answer: The herd is sold through Orbolo’s trading desk at market prices, and your return is paid out.

closing.releaseLine: Released at 60%. No capital before then.
